setup_summary.text: Fiscal Q3 FY27 is reported 2026-12-01 after the close. Consensus is EPS $3.47 and revenue $11.57B. That implies +12.8% year-on-year revenue growth against $10.26B a year earlier, versus +10.8% in Q2.
The stock has averaged a ±6.8% closing move over the last 8 reports. No options-implied move or whisper is available yet.

Q2 FY27 revenue was $11.345B (+10.8%). Operating income was flat at $2.33B, so operating margin fell to 20.5% from 22.8%. GAAP diluted EPS of $4.29 (vs $1.96) included $2.6B of strategic-investment gains.
Informatica, acquired in November 2025, contributed about $456M of Q2 revenue. Excluding it, Q2 revenue growth was roughly +6.4% (derived: $10,889M vs $10,236M).

The mix is shifting toward data. Data 360, Headless Platform and Other grew 20% to $3,618M. Agentforce Apps, 67% of subscription revenue, grew 8% to $7,193M. Professional services fell 4%, on less demand for large multi-year transformations that may continue.

Balance-sheet leverage and buybacks stepped up. Debt principal rose to $39.5B from $14.5B after $25B of March 2026 notes funded a $25B accelerated share repurchase. Interest expense was $473M in Q2 vs $67M a year earlier. Weighted basic shares fell to 820M from 956M.
Current RPO was $33.5B at 31 July 2026, up 14% year on year, with minimal FX impact. At 31 January it was up 16% including a roughly 3-point FX tailwind.
CRM fell about 5.5% on 29 October to roughly $228.72. ServiceNow dropped sharply on slower contract growth and the software group sold off. Market cap is about $190B.

last_reported.text: Q2 FY27 revenue was $11.345B (+10.8% y/y). Q1 was about $11.13B (six-month $22.48B less Q2), so Q2 was +1.9% sequential.

consensus.text: Consensus is $11.57B, or +12.8% y/y and about +2.0% sequential from Q2.

view.text: The bar needs acceleration. Holding Informatica flat at about $456M, consensus implies ex-Informatica growth of about +8% vs about +6.4% in Q2. Q3 FY26 was only +0.2% sequential over Q2 FY26, so the sequential step is above last year's pattern. Term-license revenue (4% of subscription revenue in Q2 vs 6% a year ago) is a lumpy swing factor.

view.text: This is the growth engine, but the y/y rate is flattered because Informatica is not in the prior-year base. Informatica's inorganic contribution rolls off in Q4. Watch the sequential dollar increase from $3,618M.

view.text: Growth has been steady near 8%, the same rate as the Sales and Service lines in FY26. Any move above 8% would be the clearest sign that Agentforce monetization is lifting the core apps.

last_reported.text: cRPO was $33.5B, +14% y/y, with minimal FX impact. In January it was $35.1B, +16% y/y including about 3 points of FX tailwind.

view.text: Excluding the January FX tailwind, cRPO growth was roughly 13% in constant currency, so the 14% in July is a modest constant-currency improvement. cRPO includes Informatica, so a y/y rate at or above 14% is the likely bar. The prior-year October cRPO base is not in the sources.

last_reported.text: Q2 operating margin was 20.5% vs 22.8% a year ago. Subscription cost of revenue rose to $2,021M from $1,645M. Intangible amortization in cost of revenue and S&M was $522M vs $380M. Restructuring was $94M vs $4M.

view.text: Margin pressure comes from hosting and generative-AI delivery costs, Informatica amortization and restructuring. Management says S&M and G&A should fall as a percentage of revenue over time. Q3 needs to show gross margin (77% in Q2 vs 78%) stabilizing. last_reported.text: Q2 GAAP diluted EPS was $4.29, including $2.6B of strategic-investment gains. Q3 FY26 GAAP diluted EPS was $2.19.

consensus.text: Consensus is $3.47 (Finnhub). Zacks shows $3.43, +5.5% y/y. The derived +58.5% growth in F.80 compares the consensus with prior-year GAAP EPS, so the bases do not match. Zacks' +5.5% suggests a non-GAAP consensus.

view.text: Treat the headline EPS comparison as adjusted. GAAP EPS can diverge widely, because investment gains were $2.87 per share in the first half. Anthropic marks, $473M of quarterly interest and a lower share count all move it.

last_reported.text: Q2 interest expense was $473M vs $67M. Other income was $81M vs $135M, on lower marketable-securities income ($97M vs $150M).

view.text: Management expects higher interest expense y/y throughout FY27. With fixed-rate notes and a $6B term loan, Q3 should run near Q2's $473M. Fin ($3.6B) and Contentful ($1.5B) cash closings in Q3 would reduce cash earning interest.

last_reported.text: Q2 net gains were $2,613M, driven by $2.7B of unrealized Anthropic gains. Anthropic is about $5.1B, or 45% of the $11.3B portfolio.

view.text: Gains are non-operating and unpredictable. They are recorded only on observable transactions or impairment. A 10% enterprise-value drop in the five largest holdings would cut carrying value by about $641M.

since_filing.text: On 20 October Salesforce agreed to acquire Braze (BRZE) for about $5.66B enterprise value, $47.50 per share in cash. It is expected to close in FY28, subject to Braze shareholder and regulatory approvals. It will be funded with cash and does not change FY27 guidance.
Braze stock jumped about 51% to $45.57 vs the $47.50 offer, a spread of roughly 4%. This is a market signal that the market expects the deal to close.

Management framed Braze as growth accretive but with near-term profitability dilution, with 'no change to FY30 framework.' The investor deck lists 'appropriate valuation' and 'use of balance sheet / non-dilutive form of consideration' among its criteria.

Stacked cash M&A now totals about $10.8B: Braze $5.66B, Fin $3.6B and Contentful $1.5B. On 29 October a further deal was reported, Rune Technologies (defense tech, for the Missionforce business); its terms are not in the excerpt.

On 29 October CRM fell about 5.5% to roughly $228.72 as ServiceNow tumbled on slower contract growth. The read-across to enterprise software demand is negative going into the print. IBD notes shares are below their 50-day line for the first time since July.

The 10-K (March) said the G.G. Backpage trial was expected in fall 2026. The 10-Q (August) drops that language and says the G.G. consolidated cases are stayed pending the Backpage criminal proceedings, with a reconsideration motion pending. The 10-Q is newer.
As of the 10-Q, no repurchases had been made after 31 July. $22.9B of the $50B authorization remains.
Zacks puts Q3 EPS at $3.43 (+5.5% y/y), with the FY27 consensus at $16.72 and the FY28 consensus at $16.03 (-4.1%). Finnhub's Q3 consensus is $3.47. Neither basis is stated.

key_debates.question: Can revenue growth accelerate to the ~12.8% consensus implies, given organic growth of about 6%?

bull.text: Data 360 and Headless Platform grew 20%, Informatica adds roughly $450M or more, and cRPO growth of 14% (constant-currency improvement vs January) points to firm demand. A full inorganic contribution is already embedded in the consensus step-up.

bear.text: Q2 organic growth was only about 6.4% and Agentforce Apps grew 8%. Professional services are shrinking, and term-license revenue is lower (4% of subscription revenue vs 6%). Consensus needs about 8% ex-Informatica, while last year's Q2-to-Q3 sequential step was +0.2%. ServiceNow's contract-growth warning hit the group.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 revenue vs $11.57B, the Informatica contribution disclosed in the 10-Q, ex-Informatica growth of 8% or better, and cRPO growth vs 14%.

key_debates.question: Is operating margin heading back up, or is AI and acquisition cost structurally lowering it?

bull.text: Management expects S&M and G&A to fall as a percentage of revenue through self-serve, partner channels and AI productivity. Restructuring charges should fade, and G&A was flat in dollars in Q2.

bear.text: Q2 operating margin fell 2.3 points y/y because of hosting and generative-AI delivery costs, higher intangible amortization and restructuring. Subscription cost of revenue rose about 23% vs revenue growth of 11%. New acquisitions add amortization and management admits near-term profitability dilution.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 gross margin vs 77%, GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin, and any FY27 margin guide change.

key_debates.question: Is the leveraged buyback plus serial M&A value-creating?

bull.text: The ASR cut basic shares about 14% y/y and added $0.57 to first-half EPS. Acquisitions (Fin, Contentful, Braze) extend the agentic and data roadmap and are funded without issuing equity.

bear.text: Debt rose to $39.5B, and quarterly interest expense is about $473M. About $10.8B of cash acquisitions and a $25B buyback shrink the liquidity cushion ($11.4B). Management concedes near-term profit dilution, and the ASR may require extra shares or cash at settlement.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Funding plan for Fin, Contentful and Braze (cash vs new debt), the ASR final settlement share count, and the credit-rating and capital-return commentary.

key_debates.question: How much of reported earnings is strategic-investment marks rather than operations?

bull.text: The $5.1B Anthropic stake is marked on observable transactions and adds balance-sheet value of $11.3B across 450+ investments, which could be monetized or used for ecosystem leverage.

bear.text: Gains of $2.6B in Q2 lifted GAAP EPS by $2.87 in the first half. The portfolio is concentrated (Anthropic 45%), unrealized and can reverse with impairments. The adjusted consensus excludes this volatility, so GAAP EPS headlines will be noisy.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 gains or losses line, any Anthropic funding round or other observable transactions, and the split of GAAP vs adjusted EPS.

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Revenue lands near $11.57B (+2% sequential), with Data 360 around 20% growth and Agentforce Apps about 8%. EPS is in line on adjusted terms, interest stays near $473M, and FY27 guidance is maintained. Reaction is muted to moderate.

triggers: Revenue and EPS within about 1% of consensus

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Organic growth stays near the Q2 level of about 6%, so revenue misses the step-up. cRPO growth slips below 14%, margin compression persists and the market extends the software-sector derating. Funding and dilution from the M&A program weigh on the multiple.

triggers: Weak guide or higher interest or acquisition costs

claim.text: Demand and AI-disruption risk. Agentforce Apps are growing only 8%, and AI-native competitors could bypass traditional workflows. ServiceNow's slower contract-growth outlook raised sector-wide concern into the print.

Leverage and capital allocation. Debt of $39.5B, about $473M of quarterly interest, and $10B+ of announced cash acquisitions reduce flexibility. The ASR final settlement may require delivering shares or cash depending on the stock price.
Strategic-investment concentration. Anthropic is 45% of the $11.3B portfolio. A decline in valuations or impairments would hit GAAP results, and gains are non-recurring.

Rising AI delivery costs and reliance on third-party frontier models. Hosting and generative-AI spend lifted cost of revenue. The 10-Q adds that access to frontier AI models could be suspended or restricted by providers or governments.
AI-accelerated cyber threats. The 10-Q newly warns that frontier AI could find zero-day vulnerabilities faster, compress patching time and force emergency patching.

Consumption-based pricing for Agentforce and Data 360 makes churn, pricing and revenue forecasting harder. The 10-Q adds language that AI-driven consumption models could complicate attrition prediction and pricing optimization.

Backpage litigation keeps widening. New plaintiffs and cases were added (for example, 16 Central District of California cases transferred in June and July 2026). Many are stayed under 18 U.S.C. § 1595(b), but exposure is unquantified, and a reconsideration motion on the G.G. stay is pending.

Integration and regulatory risk across Informatica, Qualified, Fin, Contentful and Braze. Regulatory approvals could delay or block the Q3 closings and the Braze deal. Informatica inorganic growth rolls off after Q3.

Data residency and sovereignty requirements may add cost or limit resiliency options. The 10-Q newly describes pre-approval requirements for emergency data migration and local-infrastructure conditions.

questions_for_management.question: What organic growth rate, excluding Informatica, is embedded in the Q3 and FY27 guidance, and what drives acceleration from about 6% in Q2?

why.text: Consensus implies about +8% ex-Informatica growth in Q3 vs about +6.4% in Q2.

questions_for_management.question: How are Agentforce and Data 360 consumption and Flex Credits trending, and when do they show up in revenue rather than cRPO?

why.text: Both are consumption-based and still 'relatively new and uncertain'. Data 360 and Headless Platform grew 20% while Agentforce Apps grew 8%.

questions_for_management.question: How will Fin, Contentful and Braze be funded? Will you add debt, how will cash fall, and what is the expected leverage and rating impact?

why.text: Roughly $10.8B of announced cash deals follow a $25B debt-funded ASR. Liquidity is $11.4B, debt principal is $39.5B and Braze is 'funded via cash'.

questions_for_management.question: What is the expected size of the remaining ASR delivery, and will buybacks resume in Q3 and Q4?

why.text: The ASR settles in Q3, no open-market repurchases occurred in Q2, and $22.9B of authorization remains.

questions_for_management.question: How much margin dilution should we expect from Informatica, Fin, Contentful and Braze, and what is the FY27 operating margin trajectory?

why.text: Q2 operating margin fell 2.3 points y/y. Management cites near-term profitability dilution from Braze and expects FY27 guidance to be unchanged.

questions_for_management.question: How should we treat strategic-investment gains, particularly Anthropic, in capital allocation and guidance? Are monetization or financing events expected?

why.text: Q2 gains were $2.6B and Anthropic is 45% of the portfolio, so GAAP EPS is highly volatile.

questions_for_management.question: What are the hosting and AI inference cost trends, and how much gross-margin pressure is in the outlook?

why.text: Subscription cost of revenue rose about 23% in Q2, driven by hosting and generative-AI spend, and gross margin slipped to 77% from 78%.

questions_for_management.question: What is the current status and timeline of the Backpage cases, including the G.G. trial date and any reserve?

why.text: The 10-K cited a fall 2026 trial. The 10-Q dropped that language and describes stays, while plaintiff numbers have grown.
